title: Identification of pyrazolo-piperidinone derivatives targeting YAP-TEAD interface 3 as anticancer agents through integrated virtual screening and mass spectrometry proteomics.
authors: Scalvini, Laura; Tagliazucchi, Lorenzo; Elisi, Gian Marco; Zappaterra, Dana; Moschella, Maria Gaetana; Fantini, Sebastian; Aiello, Daniele; Guerrini, Remo; Albanese, Valentina; Pacifico, Salvatore; Lopresti, Ludovica; Malpezzi, Giulia; Saporito, Giulia; Ferrari, Stefania; Lamesta, Michele; Losi, Lorena; Pozzi, Cecilia; Mangani, Stefano; Marverti, Gaetano; Venturelli, Alberto; Ponterini, Glauco; D'Arca, Domenico; Mor, Marco; Costi, Maria Paola
one_liner_zh: 该文通过虚拟筛选、分子动力学和质谱蛋白质组学鉴定靶向YAP-TEAD界面3的吡唑哌啶酮类抗癌化合物，属于蛋白质-DNA互作（转录因子TEAD-DNA）相关药物发现，但核心是蛋白-蛋白界面抑制而非TF-DNA结合建模，方法可迁移但非直接聚焦。
abstract: The transcriptional activity of TEAD4 (transcriptional enhancer associated domain proteins), one of the final effectors of the Hippo pathway, can be dysregulated or mutated in cancer. Consequently, targeting the interaction between TEAD and its co-activator YAP (Yes Associated Protein) to disrupt the YAP:TEAD (Y:T) heterodimer has emerged as a promising anti-cancer strategy. Therefore, in this study, we aimed to identify novel scaffolds targeting the TEAD Interface 3 surface as effective anticancer agents against colorectal and ovarian cancer. Employing virtual screening, molecular dynamics, computational ADME-T prediction, and synthetic chemistry, we initially identified novel pyrazolo-piperidinone compounds exhibiting binding affinities (K(d)) between 0.6 and 10 muM towards TEAD4 Interface 3 in a fluorescence anisotropy assay, with 6a as the initial lead for a library of 20 compounds. A few of them demonstrated effective and well-characterized cellular antiproliferative activity against HCT116 and A2780 cancer cells. They demonstrated efficacy against colorectal cancer cells resistant to the KRAS-dependent clinical candidate IAG933 and confirmed the ability to inhibit TEAD4 target genes expression. Mass spectrometry-based proteomics of HCT116 cells treated with verteporfin and 6a analogs revealed a proteome modulation consistent with an anti-TEAD mechanism of action, revealing the downregulation of CTGF and TGF-beta1. Bioinformatic metabolic pathway analysis further differentiated the mechanism of action of the 6a analogs from verteporfin, a known indirect modulator of the Y:T complex. These findings establish the pyrazolo-piperidinone class as novel Y:T disruptors and provide insights into their metabolic impact on downstream effectors, offering a valuable framework for future hit-to-lead optimization and mechanism of action studies.
abstract_zh: TEAD4（转录增强子相关结构域蛋白）是Hippo通路的最终效应因子之一，其转录活性在癌症中可能发生失调或突变。因此，靶向TEAD与其共激活因子YAP（Yes相关蛋白）之间的相互作用以破坏YAP:TEAD（Y:T）异二聚体，已成为一种有前景的抗癌策略。为此，在本研究中，我们旨在识别靶向TEAD Interface 3表面的新型骨架，作为针对结直肠癌和卵巢癌的有效抗癌剂。通过虚拟筛选、分子动力学（molecular dynamics）、计算ADME-T预测和合成化学，我们初步识别出新型吡唑并哌啶酮化合物，其在荧光各向异性测定中对TEAD4 Interface 3表现出0.6至10 μM的结合亲和力（K(d)），其中6a作为20个化合物库的初始先导物。其中一些化合物对HCT116和A2780癌细胞表现出有效且特征明确的细胞抗增殖活性。它们对耐KRAS依赖性临床候选药物IAG933的结直肠癌细胞显示出疗效，并证实了抑制TEAD4靶基因表达的能力。基于质谱的蛋白质组学分析显示，经维替泊芬（verteporfin）和6a类似物处理的HCT116细胞中，蛋白质组调节与抗TEAD作用机制一致，揭示了CTGF和TGF-β1的下调。生物信息学代谢通路分析进一步区分了6a类似物与维替泊芬（一种已知的Y:T复合物间接调节剂）的作用机制。这些发现确立了吡唑并哌啶酮类化合物作为新型Y:T破坏剂，并提供了对其下游效应因子代谢影响的见解，为未来的先导物优化和作用机制研究提供了有价值的框架。
